entities.name: Aryl O-demethylation
observations: Reactant-to-product change is selective conversion of an aryl methyl ether (Ar–OCH3) to the corresponding phenol (Ar–OH).
The methyl ester, aryl fluoride, and tert-butyl-containing scaffold are retained.
Closest database precedent uses BBr3 in dichloromethane for this selective transformation.

entities.name: Boron tribromide
observations: Boron tribromide in dichloromethane is the most practical supported reagent set for selective aryl O-demethylation while preserving the methyl ester.

entities.name: BBr3 in CH2Cl2
observations: Typical conditions are dry dichloromethane under inert atmosphere, low-temperature addition, warming toward room temperature, and careful aqueous or methanol quench.
A practical starting range is approximately 1–2 equivalents of BBr3 per aryl methyl ether.

entities.name: Aluminum hydride mixture
observations: An aluminum hydride/lithium-sodium hydroxide-type mixture in tetrahydrofuran can form the phenol but also reduces the methyl ester to a benzyl alcohol.
This reagent class is unsuitable when ester retention is required.
